claims.exact_statement: Let h be the Boolean sign gate on six uniform physical inputs negative at binary indices {0,1,2,4,8,16,32,6,17,40}, with zero bits encoding +1. Define g0=h, g1=h(g0^6), g2=h((-g1)^6), and g3=h(g2^6), each substitution on six identical disjoint copies. Then g3 is an actual 1296-bit transitive Boolean function with 0<p_min(g3)<1/16 and E(g3)>669/200, where E is the minimum relevant-coordinate conditional Fourier erasure entropy divided by its physical influence, in bits. Both 7776-bit children h(g3^6) and h((-g3)^6) have E<669/200, and both corresponding signed recentered reserves are strictly negative at every physical coordinate. Hence common-sign six-bit admission does not preserve the fixed threshold 669/200 even on high-E actual cores. Moreover, for any actual core with minority probability 0<s<=1/16, either common output orientation in this substitution gives 0<s_next<=12s^2<=(3/4)s, so this rare bias sector is absorbing under every future sign sequence.
hypotheses: Uniform independent physical inputs; actual sign outputs; entropies in bits
Six identical disjoint copies at each substitution; only one common output sign chosen for all six copies
All relevant physical coordinates included; E excludes zero-influence coordinates
No asserted unbounded H/I, arbitrary-block-sign policy, larger fixed-threshold failure, or all-depth entropy payment
proof_dependencies: Integer Walsh/edge identities for the actual h truth table
Signed paired-row disjoint composition and full hierarchical entropy identity (independently derived here)
Positive atanh-series logarithm remainder and exact rational endpoint comparisons
Explicit alpha polynomial and elementary rare-sector bounds

review_records.kind: Analytic reconstruction plus actual conditional-section/physical-edge arithmetic; exact finite circuit certificate, pilot and full pass

refutes: Candidate extension: for every actual high-E core E(g)>=K6 some common output sign makes E(h(g^6))>=E(g)
Candidate fixed-threshold implication at K=669/200: E(g)>K implies E(h((sigma*g)^6))>K for some common sigma
Candidate exclusion: every actual core with E>=K6 has p_min>=1/16
